concepts.title: Distribution of Key Minerals
concepts.definition: Metallic minerals like iron, manganese, bauxite and copper occur mainly in the peninsular plateau's old crystalline rocks, and over 97 per cent of coal reserves lie in the valleys of Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi and Godavari, making mineral geography highly concentrated.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the valley share of coal from 100 gives the coal lying outside these valleys.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy205.txt distribution of minerals and coal reserves (over 97 per cent in valleys)
question_patterns: where do India's metallic minerals mainly occur
compute the coal share outside the great valleys
name the coal-bearing valleys of peninsular India
why does bauxite suit plateau regions
state the distribution of manganese
relate geology to mineral concentration

solution_steps.explain: over 97 per cent of coal reserves lie in the valleys
the remainder is coal outside these valleys

concepts.title: Ferrous, Non-ferrous and Non-metallic Minerals
concepts.definition: Ferrous minerals - iron ore, manganese, chromite and nickel - form the backbone of metallurgical industries; non-ferrous minerals like copper, bauxite and lead feed electrical and manufacturing uses, while mica and limestone lead non-metallic minerals.
concepts.key_idea: Iron ore belts of Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar, Bellary-Chitradurga and Maharashtra-Goa anchor India's steel economy.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy205.txt ferrous, non-ferrous and non-metallic mineral sections
question_patterns: name India's four iron ore belts
distinguish ferrous from non-ferrous minerals with examples

describe bauxite distribution in India

solution_steps.explain: iron, manganese, chromite and nickel are ferrous; copper, bauxite and lead are non-ferrous
Odisha-Jharkhand and Durg-Bastar belts carry the richest hematite
each mineral feeds a distinct industrial chain

concepts.title: Conventional and Non-conventional Energy
concepts.definition: Conventional energy includes coal, petroleum, natural gas and hydel power, while non-conventional sources - solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, biogas - are renewable and decentralised; India's energy strategy pushes non-conventional sources to cut import dependence and pollution.
concepts.key_idea: Solar and wind energy suit India's geography, from Thar desert sun to the coastal wind corridors of Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy205.txt conventional and non-conventional energy sections
question_patterns: differentiate conventional and non-conventional energy

solution_steps.explain: coal, oil, gas and hydel are conventional; solar, wind, tidal and biogas are not
Rajasthan's sun, coastal Tamil Nadu's wind and Gulf of Khambhat's tides fit distinct sources
renewables cut imports and local pollution together

concepts.title: Conservation of Minerals and Energy
concepts.definition: Minerals are finite and non-reproducible, so conservation demands planned extraction, improved technology, recycling of metals, reduced wastage and substitution; energy conservation adds efficiency standards, mass transit and renewable substitution.
concepts.key_idea: Recycling one tonne of scrap steel saves ore, coal and energy together - conservation multiplies resources.

solution_steps.explain: minerals cannot regrow, so every tonne extracted is gone forever
efficient technology, recycling and substitution stretch the stock
transit choices and efficiency norms conserve at the demand end
